title: Canonical zeroth-homology comparisons for single-object right derived functors
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be abelian categories with ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Assume that $\mathcal C$ has enough injectives and K-injective resolutions, and let $R:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be additive and left exact. Use its total right derived functor $RR$ [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. For $M\in\mathcal C$, define $\kappa_{R,M}:H^0(RR(M[0]))\cong R(M)$ to be the canonical composite $H^0(RR(M[0]))\cong R^0R(M)\cong R(M)$, where the first comparison is computed by the ordinary injective resolution of $M$ and the second is the left-exact degree-zero comparison. If $S:\mathcal D\to\mathcal E$ is exact and additive, with $\mathcal E$ abelian and carrying its unbounded derived category, define $\kappa_{R,S,M}:H^0(D(S)(RR(M[0])))\cong S(R(M))$ to be the inverse exact-functor homology comparison followed by $S(\kappa_{R,M})$. These are specified canonical comparison isomorphisms, without asserting a normalization equation for any augmentation or other map.

    [PreservesFiniteLimits F]
    [EnoughInjectives C] (M : C) :

        (F.rightDerivedFunctor.obj ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor C 0).obj M)) ≅ F.obj M
